title: The Scope Type specification contradicts the Atlas's own six-Scope partition by referring to 5 Scopes
content:
A.1.2.2.2.3, the Type Specification for the Scope Type, is internally inconsistent about how many Scopes exist. Its Document Identifier Rules state "Scope Documents have the Document Identifiers from A.1 to A.6" — six slots — and its Type Overview opens by describing "the six nonzero Immutable Documents of the first layer of the Atlas." The same paragraph then closes: "Scope Documents define the broad boundaries, requirements and objectives of each of the 5 Atlas Scopes."

The Preamble (A.0.1.1.13) fixes six Scopes: Governance, Support, Stability, Protocol, Accessibility, and Agent. The Agent Scope reads as the most recent addition, which makes the "5" the plausible residue of an earlier five-Scope partition that was updated in two places out of three.

This is worth recording rather than dismissing as a typo, for two reasons. First, it is precisely the class of defect A.1.1.2.1 empowers the Core Facilitator to resolve — a contradiction within Atlas Documents, remediable by Atlas Interpretation. Second, the completeness claim is load-bearing: the sentence's whole function is to assert that the Scopes "together can fully cover all activities that are needed for Sky to function while maintaining its resilient equilibrium." A stale count in a completeness claim is a live hazard, because an argument that some activity falls outside all Scopes could be built on which enumeration is authoritative.

The governing fact is that the identifier rule (A.1 to A.6) and the six-document count are structural and mutually corroborating, so the "5" should be read as the error.
description: A.1.2.2.2.3 says Scope identifiers run A.1 to A.6 and covers 'the six nonzero Immutable Documents', then states they must together cover all activity across 'the 5 Atlas Scopes'.
